guide.summary: You can start on Composio's managed Gmail OAuth app with no setup. You need your own Google Cloud OAuth app for branding, dedicated quota, or extra scopes. The hard part is the scopes: most useful Gmail scopes (read, modify, compose) are restricted, which means Google verification and likely an annual third-party security assessment for a public app.

composio.note: Composio's docs list Gmail as managed OAuth. The default consent screen shows Composio, and quota is shared. The guide URL comes from the Gmail toolkit FAQ page, not from the structured credential_guide field (which was null).

need_own_app.answer: Not to prototype: the managed app works by default. For a production product, you will likely want your own app.
reasons: Consent screen shows 'Composio' instead of your app name and logo.
Shared quota on the default app can hit rate limits sooner; your own app gets dedicated quota.
Adding scopes beyond the defaults (e.g. gmail.settings.basic) can trigger 'App is blocked' on the managed app unless the client is verified for them.
You control the Google verification status of the client used by your users.

scenarios.label: Prototype or internal tool, own account or few known users
scenarios.when_this_applies: You and a few known users connect, or an app limited to your Google Workspace org. No public launch.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured; Testing publishing status needs no verification (c6)

waiting.basis: Google says verification is not required for dev/testing/staging or personal use (c6).

scenarios.approval: No Google verification. Testing mode shows an unverified-app warning, enforces a user cap, limits refresh token lifetime and allows only listed test users. Internal apps in a Workspace org may need admin approval.

scenarios.label: Public app, sensitive or non-sensitive scopes only (e.g. gmail.send, gmail.labels)
scenarios.when_this_applies: Any Google user can connect and you request only gmail.send / gmail.labels, no restricted scopes.

hands_on.basis: No measured effort; requires branding, domain verification, privacy policy, scope justification and demo video (c9, c10).

waiting.estimate: About 3-5 business days for sensitive scope verification
waiting.basis: Google doc states this typically takes 3-5 business days (c11). Brand verification automated step usually takes minutes (c12).

scenarios.approval: Brand verification, plus sensitive scope verification for gmail.send.

scenarios.label: Public app reading or modifying mail (gmail.readonly, modify, compose, metadata, mail.google.com)
scenarios.when_this_applies: Your product reads, modifies or composes user mail for any Google user.

hands_on.basis: No evidence on effort; includes the verification package plus a security assessment with a third-party assessor (c14, c15).

waiting.estimate: Unknown, Google says it can potentially take several weeks
waiting.basis: Google's restricted-scope page says it 'can potentially take several weeks' and gives no exact figure (c16). No developer-reported timelines were researched.

scenarios.approval: Restricted scope verification and, if data is accessed from or through a server, an annual CASA security assessment by a Google-approved assessor.

prerequisites.title: Google Cloud project and Google account
prerequisites.detail: You need a Cloud Console project where you configure branding, scopes and OAuth client. Keep owner/editor roles and the support/developer contact emails current.

prerequisites.title: Composio account and project
prerequisites.detail: You need a Composio dashboard to create an auth config and copy the redirect/callback URI.

prerequisites.title: For public apps: domain, homepage, privacy policy
prerequisites.detail: You must verify ownership of authorized domains in Google Search Console. The homepage must be public and the privacy policy must be hosted on the same domain and disclose how you access, use, store or share Google user data.

prerequisites.title: For public apps: demo video and scope justifications
prerequisites.detail: A video showing the OAuth grant and the use of each scope, uploaded to YouTube as Unlisted, plus a written justification for each scope and why narrower scopes won't work.

prerequisites.title: For restricted scopes: budget and time for a security assessment
prerequisites.detail: Plan for an assessor engagement, repeated at least every 12 months. Assessor cost was not researched.

steps.title: Decide scopes and pick the narrowest set
steps.detail: List the Gmail features you need and map each to the least-privileged scope. Flag which are non-sensitive, sensitive or restricted. Note gmail.metadata cannot be combined with gmail.readonly, gmail.modify or mail.google.com in the same request.
steps.done_when: You have a final scope list with sensitivity tier per scope.

steps.title: Create or choose a Google Cloud project and enable the Gmail API
steps.detail: Create a project (use a separate one for testing and production) and enable the Gmail API under APIs & Services. Wait a few minutes after enabling.
steps.done_when: Gmail API shows as enabled in the project.

steps.title: Configure the OAuth consent screen / branding and declare scopes
steps.detail: Set app name, support email, homepage and privacy policy links. Declare all scopes on the Data Access page. For prototypes leave publishing status as Testing and add test users.
steps.done_when: Branding is saved and scopes are listed on the Data Access page.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config and copy the callback URI
steps.detail: In the Composio dashboard create an auth config for Gmail using your own client ID and secret. Copy the redirect/callback URI Composio shows you; do not hard-code one. If you have not yet created the Google client, create it first (step order may swap).
steps.done_when: You have the callback URI from the Composio dashboard.

steps.title: Create the OAuth client in Google Cloud and paste the Composio callback URI
steps.detail: Create a web OAuth client in the Cloud Console, add the Composio callback URI as an authorized redirect URI, then copy the client ID and secret back into the Composio auth config. An agent can check that the pasted redirect URI matches exactly.
steps.done_when: Auth config saved with your client ID and secret.

steps.title: Test the connection with a test user
steps.detail: Connect a Gmail account listed as a test user. In Testing mode expect an unverified-app warning screen; you can proceed past it.
steps.done_when: Connection succeeds and a Composio tool call returns data.

steps.title: Draft privacy policy checklist, scope justifications and demo video script
steps.detail: An agent can draft the Limited Use-compliant privacy policy checklist, a per-scope justification including why narrower scopes are insufficient, and a video script covering the consent flow, app name, client ID in the address bar, and each scope's feature.
steps.done_when: Drafts are ready for you to review.

steps.title: Verify domain, publish homepage and privacy policy, record and upload video
steps.detail: Verify the domain in Search Console, publish the homepage and privacy policy on that domain, record the demo in English and upload it to YouTube as Unlisted.
steps.done_when: Domain verified, pages live, unlisted video link in hand.

steps.title: Run brand verification and publish branding
steps.detail: On the OAuth Branding page click Verify Branding, then Publish branding within 7 days or it must be re-run.

steps.title: Submit data access verification
steps.detail: In the Verification Center, declare scopes, add justifications and the video link, then submit. Watch the support and developer contact emails for follow-up from Google.
steps.done_when: Request shows as submitted in the Verification Center.

steps.title: Wait for Google review
steps.detail: Sensitive scopes typically take 3-5 business days. Restricted scopes can take several weeks.

steps.title: Complete the CASA security assessment
steps.detail: If restricted-scope data is accessed from or through a server, engage a Google-approved assessor. Recertify at least every 12 months.
steps.done_when: You have the assessor's Letter of Assessment accepted by Google.

steps.title: Reconnect users and check consent screen
steps.detail: After approval, confirm the consent screen shows your app name and no unverified warning, then reconnect accounts so new scopes are granted.
steps.done_when: A fresh account connects without a warning.

traps.title: Adding scopes on the managed app
traps.detail: Extra scopes beyond the defaults can cause 'App is blocked' because Google hasn't verified them for Composio's client.

traps.title: Branding verification expires in 7 days
traps.detail: If you do not publish within 7 days of a compliant result, you must verify again.

traps.title: Branding can't be edited during verification
traps.detail: You must cancel ongoing verification to change branding.

traps.title: Testing mode limits
traps.detail: Tester warning screen, user cap and limited refresh token lifetime still apply in Testing.

traps.title: Gmail API not enabled
traps.detail: Custom credentials fail with 'Gmail API has not been used in project' until the API is enabled in the owning project.

traps.title: gmail.metadata is incompatible with content scopes
traps.detail: Do not request gmail.metadata alongside gmail.readonly, gmail.modify or mail.google.com.

traps.title: Refresh token limit
traps.detail: Google's ~50 refresh tokens per account limit can cause 401s when exceeded.

blockers.symptom: 'App is blocked' or unverified-app screen when connecting
blockers.what_it_means: The client requests scopes Google hasn't verified for it.
blockers.what_to_do: Remove extra scopes, or use your own OAuth app and submit the scopes for verification. For Testing mode, add the user as a test user.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare your auth config scopes against the defaults and list which ones are sensitive or restricted.

blockers.what_it_means: Your app uses restricted scopes and handles the data on a server.
blockers.what_to_do: Engage a Google-approved CASA assessor, or reduce scopes to non-restricted ones if your feature allows.
blockers.agent_can_help: Review whether a narrower scope meets your use case and draft the 'why narrower scopes aren't sufficient' text.

blockers.what_it_means: Scopes are invalid or badly formatted in the authorization URL.
blockers.what_to_do: Check scope strings against Google's docs and your auth config.
blockers.agent_can_help: Validate the scope strings in your auth config.

blockers.symptom: Quota exhausted or rate limit errors
blockers.what_it_means: On the managed app you share quota with other users.
blockers.what_to_do: Use your own OAuth app and add exponential backoff.

blockers.symptom: Workspace users can't authorize your app
blockers.what_it_means: Workspace admins may restrict sensitive scopes to trusted OAuth client IDs.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the customer's admin to mark your client ID as trusted.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft an admin-facing request with your client ID and scopes.

open_questions: Exact duration of restricted-scope review plus CASA: not stated in docs; ask Google via the Verification Center or find developer reports.
Whether Composio-brokered token storage counts as 'storing restricted data on your servers' for your app: not verified; ask Composio and Google.
Which scopes Composio's managed app is verified for: only inferred from the FAQ.
Exact user cap for unverified apps: not given in the pages read.

claims.text: Gmail is in Composio's managed OAuth list, so Composio can provide the OAuth app.
claims.quote: Composio can provide the OAuth app that your users authorize when they connect a toolkit.
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: By default the consent screen shows Composio's OAuth app; your own app is needed to show your name and logo.
claims.quote: By default, the consent screen uses Composio's OAuth app.
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: Adding extra scopes beyond defaults on the managed client can cause 'App is blocked'.
claims.quote: The OAuth client is requesting scopes that Google hasn't verified for that client.
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: Composio says to create your own app and submit scopes for verification if blocked.
claims.quote: Remove the additional scopes from your auth config, or create your own OAuth app and submit the scopes for verification.
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: Default Composio app shares quota; your own app gives dedicated quota.
claims.quote: Use your own OAuth app credentials to get a dedicated quota, and add exponential backoff and retries to handle transient rate limits.
claims.label: composio_docs

claims.text: Apps in development/testing can stay in Testing publishing status, limited to listed test users, without verification.
claims.quote: Therefore, if your app is in the development, testing, or staging phases, verification isn't required.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: In Testing, a tester warning screen, user cap and limited refresh token lifetime still apply.
claims.quote: Note: Your app is still subject to a tester warning screen, as shown in figure 2, a user cap is in effect, and the refresh token lifetime is limited.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Internal-use apps need an Internal user type in an org-owned project and might need admin approval.
claims.quote: In this case, your app might need approval from an organization administrator.
claims.label: provider_docs

claims.text: Verification requires domain ownership verified in Search Console and a public homepage.
claims.quote: Your home page must be publicly accessible, and not just accessible to your site's logged-in users.
claims.label: provider_docs
